# Backend Runtime integration and managed proof

This reference covers the closed Runtime HTTP boundary, Action invocation, managed Runtime proof, and backend Handler coding idioms. Capability discovery comes from the CLI-compiled authority contract; frontend dependency installation and package wiring are outside this Skill.

## Closed HTTP boundary

Project-owned backend source must not add, register, proxy, or require any application-facing HTTP interface. Do not create a project-local HTTP handler, router, controller, middleware endpoint, BFF, API proxy, serverless function, or alternate transport route. Application-facing client selection and wiring belong to the frontend owner outside this Skill; Builder models only the Application Delivery-published `runtime-domain-api-v1` contract.

Custom source-owned Action Handlers expose no separate HTTP route; Runtime invokes them only through the published object or record Action operations below. Connector providers may perform contract-declared outbound calls through generated Connector APIs and governed transport, but they must not publish an inbound project API. If the published Runtime CRUD, Action, Report, file, authentication, or Connector contracts cannot express a required behavior, record the exact platform-owner finding and repair that owner in the same session instead of adding an HTTP endpoint; only the terminal policy's proved unrecoverable conditions permit stopping.

## Action invocation

Select object versus record invocation from the Runtime-published Action `kind`, using `runtimeActionInvocationScope`; never infer it from UI layout or from whether the execution owner is a custom Handler.

- `object_create`, `object_operation`, and `bulk_operation` use `runObjectAction` at `POST /objects/{objectKey}/actions/{actionKey}/run`.
- `record_update`, `record_delete`, `record_restore`, `transition_state`, `conditional_update`, and `record_operation` use `runRecordAction` at `POST /objects/{objectKey}/records/{recordID}/actions/{actionKey}`.

Backend acceptance wraps typed Action input as `{"data": <payload>}`; a bare payload is invalid for the Action invocation contract.

Call `listActions(objectKey)` first and pass the returned full `action_definition.key` unchanged to `runObjectAction` or `runRecordAction`; never shorten `group_class.book_group_class` to `book_group_class`. Use the exact storage values published by the Action input contract, such as `member`, not translated labels such as `会员`. A `record_operation` also requires the existing record ID in the record route; the presence of a button on an object list does not turn it into an object Action.

Frontends never call a generated Handler directly. Preserve the bounded Action input/output contract, workspace, Product Surface, bearer identity, request ID, idempotency key, assurance token, and concurrency value. Preserve Runtime result references and triggered workflows instead of reducing the response to a success boolean.

One accepted business intent must produce one Runtime mutation request (gate: G04). For example, “open table” is one declared Action call, not `create table session` followed by separate status, occupancy, audit, and notification mutations. Do not use `Promise.all`, sequential mutation hooks, retries with new keys, or a browser-side rollback to assemble one atomic backend command. Put the complete typed input on the Action and let its Runtime-owned unit of work perform all effects. Refetch/invalidation after the response and polling a returned job are allowed reads; they must not hide additional writes.

## Managed Runtime proof

For normal whole-project work, start and inspect the Runtime through separate managed Runtime start/status Gates in the current Host/Agent session TODO, using the packaged CLI, current project-relative bundle, and an explicit numeric loopback address such as `127.0.0.1:<dedicated-port>`. The Gate runner validates the exact argv and source/Runtime/cohort bindings and requires the `domainry-managed-runtime-process-v3` response/receipt. A failed start or status Gate remains immutable evidence: diagnose it, repair the owner, append a uniquely labeled repair-round Gate pair to the same TODO, sync, rerun, and continue. Neither Gate closes the broader acceptance-session and differentiated-data readiness item.

Use the machine-owned `runtime-process-continuation` profile only for a caller-explicit standalone recovery after an earlier Agent task has ended. Its compact TODO and returned recipes are not the normal whole-project phase transition. Stop with `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" runtime-process stop --project <project>` after acceptance. The managed receipt records the address, so subsequent acceptance commands use the same Runtime cohort. Never background-launch, discover arbitrary PIDs, kill unrelated processes, or assemble Runtime Gate controls by hand.

Runtime proof must cover declared allowed, denied, and scoped actors; Action effects; conditional conflicts; transaction rollback; idempotent replay without a second mutation or receipt; workflows/outbox; durable audit; and current delivery/package/Runtime receipt identity. Use task-published database evidence paths; do not rediscover private schema.

Stop Runtime and reclaim ports and processes after scenarios. A running process, local HTTP response, or browser screenshot without matching delivery, package, and Runtime identity is not release evidence.

## Handler coding idioms (validated against the live Runtime)

These idioms come from real Handler defects observed at runtime; `project source finalize`, compile, tests, and `project check` do NOT catch any of them.

**Finalizer source-contract preflight.** Unlike the idioms below, `project source finalize` DOES reject the following three contracts (`backend_technical_contract` check), so each violation costs a failed-finalize round-trip — one real run hit 8 violations at once. Check every Handler before finalizing: (1) no generated capability I/O inside any loop (`for`/`range`) or recursive call cycle — do pure selection into bounded slices and call the generated batch/query capability once outside the loop; (2) every List query declares `Page(page, pageSize)` with a literal page size from 1 through 200 — an unpaged first result is forbidden; (3) no discarded call result or error — assign every capability return and handle every error. Generated batch inputs are 1 through 200, ordered one-to-one, and inherit the Action Workspace, Principal, grants, Scope, and transaction. Minimal accepted fan-out shape:

```go
// Pure selection: capability I/O only outside loops.
orders, err := caps.RepairOrder.List(ctx, data.NewRepairOrderQuery().
    WhereStatusEqual(schema.RepairOrderStatusDispatched).
    OrderByIDAscending().
    Page(1, 200)) // literal page size, 1..200
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
pending := make([]schema.RepairOrder, 0, runCapacity)
for _, order := range orders { // pure filtering loop: no capability calls here
    if len(pending) == runCapacity {
        break
    }
    if eligible(order) {
        pending = append(pending, order)
    }
}
queries := make([]data.DispatchReceiptQuery, len(pending))
for index, order := range pending { // pure request construction only
    queries[index] = data.NewDispatchReceiptQuery().
        WhereOrderIDEqual(order.ID).
        WhereBusinessDateEqual(businessDate)
}
exists, err := caps.DispatchReceipt.ExistsBatch(ctx, queries) // one call, outside loops
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
// Build CreateBatch and notification DispatchBatch inputs in pure loops, then
// invoke each batch once outside loops and return every error unchanged.
```

**Build tag.** Backend compile requires the Domain SDK build constraint: a plain `go build ./...` fails on `verifiedDomainSDKBuildConstraint`. The tag is published as `schema.DomainSDKBuildConstraint` in the generated schema package's revision constants; run all backend commands as `go build|vet|test -tags "$(go run ./cmd/... 2>/dev/null || grep -roh 'domainry_domain_sdk_[a-f0-9]*' backend/generated/ | head -1)" ./...` — or read the constant from `backend/generated/schema/revision.gen.go`. The CLI's own `project verify` supplies the tag automatically; only manual Go commands need it.

**ConditionalUpdate requires a real condition.** A `conditional_update` Handler mutation without a compare-and-set token or predicate fails at runtime with `backend.generated.conditional_mutation_required`. Attach the condition observed under `GetForUpdate`:

```go
mutation := data.NewTicketUpdate(ticket.ID).SetAssigneeID(assignee)
if ticket.AssigneeID == nil {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDNull("ticket.assign.conflict")
} else {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDEqual(*ticket.AssigneeID, "ticket.assign.conflict")
}
updated, err := caps.Ticket.ConditionalUpdate(ctx, mutation)
```

`Require<Field>Equal/NotEqual/Null(errorCode)` predicates and `WithExpectedUpdatedAt(...)` are the generated condition surface (arithmetic `Increment*`/`Decrement*` effects are inherently compare-and-set and also satisfy the requirement). On idempotent replay the predicate legitimately differs (equal-to-current instead of null); test assertions must compare per-execution expected mutations, not demand identical mutations.

The generated data package exports `ValidateConditionalMutation`, and both the real data layer and the scaffolded fakes enforce it — a mutation with no condition fails unit tests with `backend.generated.conditional_mutation_required`. A hand-written fake must route through the same helper; never write one that accepts an unconditional mutation. As a cheap belt-and-suspenders guard for call sites no unit case exercises, after implementing each module and before `project source finalize`, run the static self-check from the project root and require exit code 0 (`grep -L` alone does not encode the verdict in its exit status, so the wrapper below is the command to bind as Gate evidence):

```bash
bash -c 'viol=$(grep -rl --include="*.go" -e ".ConditionalUpdate(" backend | grep -v "/generated/" | grep -v "_test\.go" | xargs -r grep -LE "Require[A-Za-z]+\(|WithExpectedUpdatedAt\(|Increment[A-Za-z]*\(|Decrement[A-Za-z]*\("); [ -z "$viol" ] || { echo "$viol"; exit 1; }'
```

Exit 1 lists every file that builds a `ConditionalUpdate` with no condition anywhere in that file; each will fail live with `backend.generated.conditional_mutation_required`. The check is file-granular: a file that mixes one conditioned and one bare call still passes, so keep one handler per file (the default layout). The development TODO template carries this as a required implementation-stage checkbox — bind it with `... run <gate-id> --bind source --` followed by the command above verbatim (it already starts with `bash -c`).

**NotificationIntent.SubjectVersion must be non-empty.** `runtimeext.NotificationIntent` fails `backend.notification.action_intent_invalid` when `SubjectVersion` is empty. Generated typed reads and mutation results expose `UpdatedAt`; mutation results receive it from the same canonical staged commit that Runtime persists. Use the subject record's `UpdatedAt` (including the value returned by `ConditionalUpdate`) as `SubjectVersion`; do not substitute transport metadata such as `request_id`, leave the field empty, or skip the dispatch.

**Transition Actions from Handlers or probes** must send the target state in the request payload (see `crud-and-state-machine.md`): a payload-less transition fails closed with 400 `backend.action.transition_payload_required`.
# Verification evidence levels

Use this ladder for every verify Gate and final claim. Each level includes the lower levels, but an artifact reaches a level only when its current proof exists and is bound to the current source/model/Runtime identity.

## Ladder

- `L0_declared`: the capability exists in requirements, model metadata, or source. This proves intent only.
- `L1_delivery_verified`: source finalization is current; format, lint, vet, tests, `project verify`, and packaging pass. This proves structural/release closure, not behavior.
- `L2_api_verified`: the operation executes through the real managed Runtime with a real session and its durable result is read back through the typed API or database. A denied/error/conflict case proves unchanged durable state; an idempotency case proves one effect after replay.
- `L3_scenario_verified`: every in-scope backend acceptance journey executes end to end on real Runtime data across its complete role/case matrix. Each permission boundary includes allow and deny probes; each data-scope rule uses differentiated identities and records; every mutation includes persistence evidence; Workflow, Scheduler, Automation, Connector, audit, and outbox claims include their terminal observable effect.
- `L4_browser_verified`: **outside this Skill's acceptance scope.** The level number is reserved so the ladder stays stable, but browser-layer UI verification is never required, claimed, or a completion precondition here; backend delivery acceptance stops at L3/L5.
- `L5_restart_verified`: the critical L3 journey subset and sessions remain correct after a managed Runtime restart, with durable state read back and the critical cases rerun.

## Claim rules

- Never call L0/L1 output `verified`, `accepted`, `working`, `scenario_verified`, or `done`; say `declared` or `delivery_verified`.
- Never infer L2/L3 from a test name, source inspection, metadata checklist, `project verify`, package receipt, Runtime health, HTTP 2xx alone, TODO prose, or TODO checker success.
- Never count a click, toast, queued job, emitted event, waiting Workflow, metadata-only import/export record, or local state change as the terminal business effect.
- Report skipped checks as skipped. Do not fold them into a higher level.
- Report coverage only with its exact include scope. A subset percentage is not whole-project coverage.
- Treat missing, empty, partial, stale, unbound, contradictory, or hand-written summary evidence as non-passing.

## L3 evidence requirements

For every accepted operation/case row, bind project-local evidence to the current full-stack source digest and Runtime delivery identity. Record the operation, actor/role, case, request/response or execution identity, expected owner, permission and data scope, persistence probe, before/after state digest, audit/receipt identity when applicable, and result.

For non-`none` data scope, provide at least two distinguishable owners and two scope groups when the rule separates them, plus records inside and outside the actor's allowed scope. A single actor, team, owner, or record cannot prove a scope boundary.

For mutations:

- success requires different before/after state and a successful read-back;
- denied, validation, and conflict cases require identical before/after state;
- idempotent replay requires the replay state to equal the first successful after-state;
- restart persistence requires the post-restart state to equal the accepted pre-restart state.

## Minimum terminal level

Whole-project and Runtime-integrated backend completion require current L3 for every in-scope journey and L5 for every critical journey marked restart-sensitive. A light existing-project increment may reference prior current evidence for unchanged operations, but every changed operation and affected regression boundary must reach the same required level. Completion in this Skill is backend acceptance: L3 for every in-scope journey plus L5 for restart-sensitive ones; L4 browser evidence is never required. This Skill never changes frontend source, so it carries no frontend typecheck/build duty; frontend-owned defects are recorded as findings for the frontend owner.
# Verification and terminal policy

Read this file completely on entry to `verify`, `done`, or terminal review after a repair.

## Verification closure

After `project verify`, package, and startup of the exact current managed Runtime, run:

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance prepare --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

This creates the CLI-owned `.domainry/builder/acceptance/denominator.json`. Do not edit it. The denominator is generated from requirement IDs, every linked model resource, acceptance scenarios, typed Runtime operations, roles and exact data-scope declarations, plus capability-specific lifecycles. It also contains the mandatory `domainry-semantic-acceptance-contract-v1`: exactly one mapping per denominator case from requirement → actor → formal principal context → fresh setup → command operation → evidence facts → reason-specific oracle. Preparation and every later load fail closed if a mapping is missing or if its actor, command, fact closure, setup isolation, expected outcome/error, or HTTP oracle diverges from the denominator. Its hash binds the current model, Blueprint, capability lock, Runtime Domain API, delivery, Runtime manifest, verification/package receipts, Runtime binary, and stable database cohort identity. The live process PID is intentionally not part of that stable hash because a restart case must replace it; the typed restart artifact must bind the old PID, current new PID, unchanged database cohort, delivery, and binary. A model, capability, source, package, database target, or Runtime change requires a new denominator; `prepare` archives every generation under `.domainry/builder/acceptance/history/denominator/`, and previously recorded results survive an evolution only through the incremental staleness flow below — never by assumption.

The denominator must cover every changed or newly published operation plus referenced prior evidence for unchanged operations. Each case names its Runtime owner, actor/role, permission and data scope, required outcome, error contract, restart sensitivity, and required evidence kinds. Every scoped read and write requires positive and differentiated-scope proof (database-agnostic, by ordinary query/HTTP probes — never engine-level RLS posture; see G14); every protected operation also requires permission-denied proof. Writes additionally require missing-idempotency-key rejection, idempotent replay, idempotency conflict, persistence read-back and audit correlation. Project Actions additionally require one HTTP mutation per business intent, one Runtime unit of work, atomic commit, injected rollback, and concurrency conflict; atomicity is proven by `http_exchange` + `transaction_trace` + `persistence_snapshot` + `audit_correlation`. The denominator never reads frontend source or requires frontend evidence. Each declared Handler Connector call gets its own case bound to the exact connector, connection, provider, operation, execution mode and side-effect class; durable writes require worker restart and terminal reconciliation. Declared notification events require after-commit once-only durable refetch, and every external channel gets its own provider-terminal case. Every Report and typed list/search/query operation requires bounded page and stable traversal cases with a query profile captured on the same database cohort named by the managed process receipt: SQLite uses `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, MySQL uses `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON`, and PostgreSQL uses `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`, all with statement/row-count observation and machine-checked index/full-scan classification. Evidence whose dialect or plan format differs from `runtime_identity.database_driver` is rejected; no second database or SQLite fallback is allowed. Its signed cursor must either encode the complete deterministic keyset tuple or bind an authorized source version to a bounded offset; a source-version-fenced continuation must reject source drift as a stale-cursor conflict. Automation Rules derive before-transaction rollback or after-commit restart/terminal cases from their trigger. Agent resources additionally require task cancel/retry/reconcile with terminal worker/audit evidence and interactive SSE disconnect/resume. A manual approval Workflow is proven as a durable process: start before the managed Runtime replacement, refetch after restart, decide real assigned tasks through participant APIs, and observe terminal persistence/audit; it does not claim `worker_terminal` unless the graph actually schedules worker-owned work. Scheduled jobs and governed report exports retain worker restart/resume evidence. Typed operations declared by acceptance `config.runtime_operations` must resolve to the pinned Runtime API and include both positive and denied rows for writes. Read and apply all 32 families in [production-technical-gates.md](production-technical-gates.md); a project may mark a family not applicable only from model-derived evidence.

Semantic oracles are strict. Each scenario uses fresh setup identities/records or names an explicit dependency whose passing evidence is current. A positive case must identify and observe its intended target with the required non-empty facts; a `2xx` paired with an empty collection, null result, zero aggregate, or different record is not proof unless that exact value is the confirmed outcome. A negative case must reach the intended stable status/error/concealment and prove unchanged durable state; an arbitrary `4xx`, `not found`, empty result caused by bad setup, or exception from a missing dependency is not the expected rejection. Scope isolation probes use otherwise equivalent requests against the same target through formal matching and non-matching Runtime sessions, plus the broader in-scope role when applicable. Runtime-owned identity/context values in setup and requests must come from the formal typed client, seed/admin path, or persisted Runtime result and be carried unchanged; synthetic claims or hand-normalized canonical values invalidate the case.

### Runner-first acceptance execution

With the denominator prepared and the managed Runtime healthy, execute the mechanical case families through the platform runner FIRST — before writing any harness code:

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance run --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --cases standard --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
```

The runner (capability `project.acceptance.run`, diagnostic report contract `domainry-backend-acceptance-run-v2`) mechanically executes the standard Action, Automation, Report GET-summary, Runtime read-route, Workflow, governed export and Scheduler families against the live Runtime and the exact sqlite/mysql/postgres database cohort bound by its managed process receipt, validates every artifact with the same `acceptance check` validators before writing it, and atomically writes/merges one complete `domainry-backend-acceptance-results-v2` document. External cohorts require the same explicit `DATABASE_DRIVER`/`DATABASE_DSN` environment binding already used by the managed Runtime; the runner compares only non-secret DSN/cohort identities and never serializes the DSN. It contains exactly one row per denominator case: `passed`, `declared_gap`, or `not_passed` with typed responsibility. Existing passed/gap rows are immutable; existing `not_passed` rows are retried. The separate `.domainry/development/acceptance-evidence/backend-acceptance-run.json` is execution diagnostics, not a second source of case truth. For every case the runner uses the semantic contract's exact actor and calls the authenticated Runtime `GET /identity/principal-context` resolver; Runtime returns canonical workspace/workforce/organization/business-profile/surface selectors, and the runner carries only those selectors into requests. Neither runner nor business harness may infer a user from role ordering, construct profile headers, or query Runtime-owned identity tables. Never re-implement or overwrite a runner-passed case. A `not_passed` outcome with `disposition:"runtime_failed"` is an observed contract violation — a product defect to repair at its owner, never a harness problem. Only `needs_business_harness` rows belong in the self-built harness. `blocked_dependency`, `blocked_platform`, `unsupported_runner`, `setup_failed`, `evidence_rejected`, and `runtime_failed` return to their named owner first; downstream cases sharing a failed setup are `blocked_dependency`, not independent failures.

Self-built harness code must be a thin assertion layer on top of [acceptance-harness-core.py](../assets/acceptance-harness-core.py): copy that file unchanged into `.domainry/development/`, then write only per-case assertion functions against it — never re-implement session/auth bootstrap, HTTP or database capture, artifact/evidence/results writers, resume state, retry/backoff plumbing, or any DSN parser/adapter. SQLite is stdlib-backed. For MySQL, install `PyMySQL` in the harness environment and call `AcceptanceDatabase.from_runtime_state(PROJECT_ROOT, state)` (or construct `Harness` normally) with no callback: core lazy-loads PyMySQL and exclusively accepts the managed Runtime Go-style contract `user:<password>@tcp(host:port)/database?charset=utf8mb4&parseTime=True&loc=Local`. URL DSNs, omitted or invalid targets/ports, and added, reordered, unknown, or dangerous query semantics fail closed; the password may be empty and is never emitted. Agent-written MySQL connectors and DSN parsers are prohibited. PostgreSQL retains the explicit advanced DB-API 2 `database_connector(driver, dsn, schema)` boundary. For both external drivers, core reads the random in-database marker and derives `sha256("domainry-managed-runtime-database-cohort-v1\n" + driver + "\n" + receipt.database_dsn_identity_sha256 + "\n" + marker_identity)` before comparing it with the managed Runtime receipt's `database_identity_sha256`; the marker is never itself the receipt identity, and copied marker rows at a different DSN identity fail closed. Missing or invalid receipt/marker contracts and identities are rejected without fallback. Core suppresses connector stdout/stderr, owns dialect SQL/EXPLAIN and DSN/password redaction, and never falls back to SQLite. Use `harness.session_for_case(case)` exclusively for the frozen actor/principal mapping. Register cases in `ScenarioGraph`; each setup receives a fresh opaque namespace, `setup_failed` is distinct from a product failure, and downstream cases become `blocked_dependency` rather than executing against missing residue. Apply `ReasonOracle` for exact positive, rejection, state, scope, and audit assertions before sealing evidence.

Execute only the remaining `needs_business_harness` cases through that real acceptance harness and project-provisioned non-human Runtime identities. The harness—not prose editing—writes typed HTTP exchanges, SSE transcripts, durable refetches, idempotency receipts, database snapshots, transaction and pagination traces, query profiles, audit correlation, differentiated-scope data, provider receipts, worker terminal observations, and restart observations under project-owned `backend/tests/evidence/**`. Self-built harness code and every intermediate working file live under `.domainry/development/**` from the very first file, never anywhere under `backend/**`: harness files inside `backend/**` dirty the finalized `source_sha256` and make every gate receipt stale, and the measured cost of that mistake is a full finalize/verify/package redo plus re-recording all evidence. Every structured observation references one real regular non-symlink artifact and its SHA-256; persistence evidence also supplies before/after hashes and, for replay, the replay hash. Results and every evidence document bind the denominator and Runtime identity hashes. Then run:

The result document contract is `domainry-backend-acceptance-results-v2`: copy `denominator_sha256`, `runtime_identity`, and `runtime_identity_sha256` exactly from the denominator and provide exactly one `results[]` row for every denominator case. A `passed` row contains `case_id`, `state`, and `evidence[]` (`path`, `sha256`); a `not_passed` row contains no evidence and requires `outcome.disposition`, stable `code`, `owner`, `root_case_id`, `retryable`, and factual `reason`; a `declared_gap` row uses the existing typed gap contract. `acceptance check` fails closed while any `not_passed` row remains. The business harness may replace only a row whose disposition is `needs_business_harness`; it cannot replace platform, dependency, setup, evidence, unsupported-runner, or Runtime failures. Each referenced evidence document is `domainry-backend-acceptance-evidence-v1` with `state:"passed"`, the exact case/denominator/Runtime hashes, and `observations[]`. An observation has `kind`, project-relative `artifact`, `artifact_sha256`, and only for `persistence_snapshot` the required `before_sha256`/`after_sha256` plus replay SHA when applicable. Each artifact is strict JSON `domainry-backend-acceptance-artifact-v1` and binds its kind, case, operation, Runtime identity, producer source receipt, capture owner, and typed facts. Accepted kinds are `http_exchange`, `persistence_snapshot`, `idempotency_receipt`, `sse_transcript`, `durable_refetch`, `runtime_restart`, `worker_terminal`, `differentiated_scope_data`, `transaction_trace`, `pagination_trace`, `query_profile`, `audit_correlation`, `security_posture`, and `provider_receipt`. Pagination facts bind stable sort/tie-breaker and cursor strategy; offset fencing additionally requires the bound source version and observed stale-cursor rejection. Provider receipts bind the denominator's exact connector, connection, provider, operation; a durable provider or notification audit also requires its outbox reference. A correctly hashed arbitrary text file or a typed artifact whose endpoint, actor, outcome, transaction counts, page facts, process/database identity, differentiated data scope, or provider terminal state contradicts the denominator is rejected. The harness must preserve secrets safely, but redaction cannot remove facts needed to prove the case.

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance check --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
```

The check reruns model derivation, resolves the live managed Runtime cohort, verifies every raw artifact, and requires exact set equality with the denominator. Missing, orphan, duplicate, failed, stale, unbound, unknown-kind, artifactless, or `self_reported` coverage fails. A percentage, prose claim, Mock transcript, or evidence from another Runtime can never satisfy it.

### Incremental re-recording after a model evolution

The denominator's `artifact_manifest` digests each operation's dependency closure, so an evolution no longer forces a blind full re-record: evidence recorded against an archived earlier generation stays binding when a complete hash proof chain shows nothing its case depends on changed. After any evolution, with the new denominator prepared, first run:

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance stale-report --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
```

The report (contract `domainry-backend-acceptance-stale-report-v1`) classifies every case as `current` (evidence still binds), `stale` (with reason), `missing`, or `declared_gap`, plus counts. Re-record ONLY the `stale` + `missing` subset. For the runner's mechanical families, re-run `project acceptance run --cases standard` on the same results file: it applies the same per-case carry-forward proof, keeps every `current` result (report field `carried_forward`), rebinds the file to the new denominator, and re-executes only what it dropped. For the remaining stale business-assertion cases, re-record through the harness core's stale-list resume — `stale_case_ids(<stale-report>)` plus `Harness(..., stale_report=...)` and `pending_cases(...)` — which rewrites only the affected result entries (evidence file paths are reused) instead of rebuilding the results file. Then run `acceptance check` as usual: a receipt with non-zero `carried_forward_cases` is a normal, complete result — carried-forward coverage is hash-proven, never a gap and never `self_reported`.

Carry-forward pays only when the repair converges on attributable model items (actions, workflows, reports, export controls, scheduled jobs, agent tasks — plus a report's own `backend/reports/<report-key>.sql`). Any other project source change — handler code, config, anything else under `backend/**` — and any shared-collection change (objects, roles, workspaces, automation rules, seeds, ...) shifts the shared digest and makes every case stale; prefer model-item-level fixes and keep every working file out of `backend/**` (harness location discipline above).

Finish the complete verification round before repair. Preserve every first failure and continue safe checks to collect the full finding inventory. `reconcile` never replays a product command and never overwrites a stale declared pass with a failed attempt: a strictly verifiable legacy cohort may receive an explicit migration receipt, a prior pass may be restored only from intact authoritative evidence, and every other case enters the typed manual repair queue. Recoverable `repair_required` exits 0 for shell continuation; only typed unrecoverable or corrupted/unsafe input exits nonzero. Then repair the named owner, create new round-specific Gates for invalidated commands, and continue; a terminal Gate and its first receipt are never overwritten or rerun.

The CLI makes this concrete for local structural checks. A failed metadata checklist writes `.domainry/builder/receipts/checklist-failed.json`; a failed source finalization writes `.domainry/builder/receipts/finalization-failed.json`; a failed `project verify` writes `.domainry/builder/receipts/verification-failed.json`. Each check is `passed`, `failed`, or `skipped_dependency`. Safe independent checks run in the same round even when a sibling fails; dependency-bound checks are skipped explicitly. Treat every `failed` row as one repair inventory and never treat `skipped_dependency` as a pass. These receipts remain L1 structural evidence only.

Run and bind evidence for:

- protected source boundary (`frontend/**` untouched under every recorded frontend mutation scope — no frontend typecheck/test/build set exists in this Skill because it never changes frontend source), and current source finalization;
- backend format, lint, vet, focused tests, full tests, verification, and package receipts;
- exact Runtime delivery/manifest identity and healthy managed Runtime;
- real non-human acceptance sessions and differentiated seed data;
- the complete operation x role x required-case inventory;
- the current acceptance denominator and its passing exact-set check receipt;
- allowed and denied authorization, application-layer data scope, sensitive fields, durable effects, conflicts, errors, and idempotency;
- Workflow, Scheduler, Automation, Connector, audit, outbox, and external-effect terminal outcomes;
- persistence read-back and critical-case restart persistence;
- cleanup of temporary records, processes, ports, and databases.

Acceptance in this Skill verifies backend logic end-to-end — real managed-Runtime HTTP/SSE/worker/database behavior. Browser-layer UI verification is outside its acceptance scope and is never a completion precondition.

The evidence Gate must bind evidence content plus applicable source, model/Blueprint, and Runtime identities. A later identity or artifact-content change makes the Gate stale. Re-run commands or regenerate artifacts; never reattach unchanged prose.

Evidence rules — tool-produced content only: every evidence file's content must be produced by a command, script, or platform tool and carry what makes it reproducible (the recorded command line, or its source plus sha256). The model never hand-transcribes, excerpts, or re-arranges content into an evidence file. In the TODO, an `Evidence:` line carries only the gate ID and path pointers; inlining more than one line of content there is prohibited.

## Failure classification

- Missing credentials, acceptance identities, differentiated data, explicit Runtime configuration, routes, permissions, sessions, Runtime health, or persistence is normally an implementation/Foundation defect. Return it to its owner and repair it in the same session; it becomes an external blocker only when every authorized provisioning/recovery path remains unavailable with recorded evidence.
- `verification_blocked` is allowed only when implementation is complete and every authorized execution mechanism for a required check remains unavailable after all recovery paths, or when continuing would risk data corruption/security, a result-changing business ambiguity has no safe authority, or governing contracts are objectively contradictory. Name the blocked checks, recovery attempts, project-local/external evidence, and highest reached level.
- Missing, partial, skipped, failed, stale, unbound, contradictory, or insufficient behavior evidence from an ordinary round is a repair finding, not a blocker, task exit, or intentional prototype. It can become terminal `acceptance_failed` only after every evidence-supported in-scope owner repair has been exhausted and the same frozen contract still fails.
- A non-blocking limitation may be reported only when it is outside the frozen scope and does not weaken an in-scope claim.

## Terminal states

This terminal verification sequence applies to `Execution scope: implementation`. A `requirements_only` batch may move directly from closed requirements/domain-truth Gates to `done`; that state proves only the accepted requirements artifact, reports no delivery or L1-L5 implementation claim, and must not imply Runtime or UI verification.

Record exactly one state:

- `done`: every in-scope Gate has current bound evidence at the required level, the acceptance matrix is complete, the finding inventory is empty, and no requirement is hidden, downgraded, or deferred.
- `acceptance_failed`: after the same-session repair loop exhausts every evidence-supported in-scope owner repair, implementation or evidence still fails the frozen acceptance contract. A first or ordinary failed acceptance round never qualifies.
- `verification_blocked`: implementation is complete but a required check cannot execute because no authorized execution capability exists.

Only `done` permits a whole-batch completion claim. Other states report per-capability results and the highest evidence level without upward summarization. Neither state is a shortcut around diagnosis: do not record it merely because validate/apply/verify/package/Runtime/canary/acceptance returned non-zero, and do not move a recoverable repair to user wait or another Host/Agent session.

Before completion, keep `Current stage: verify`, require the evidence Gate's `verify` status to pass, and run the TODO checker with `--expected-stage verify`. Change the stage to `done` only after terminal policy permits it; then require the Gate's `done` status and run the TODO checker again immediately before the final response.

The final summary states terminal state, implemented scope, frontend mutation scope, current delivery identity, tests/builds, Runtime result, highest evidence level, restart result, and open limitations. Never imply L4 browser evidence — it is outside this Skill's acceptance scope.

# Verification and terminal policy

Read this file completely on entry to `verify`, `done`, or terminal review after a repair.

## Verification closure

After `project verify`, package, and startup of the exact current managed Runtime, run:

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance prepare --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

This creates the CLI-owned `.domainry/builder/acceptance/denominator.json`. Do not edit it. The denominator is generated from requirement IDs, every linked model resource, acceptance scenarios, typed Runtime operations, roles and exact data-scope declarations, plus capability-specific lifecycles. It also contains the mandatory `domainry-semantic-acceptance-contract-v1`: exactly one mapping per denominator case from requirement → actor → formal principal context → fresh setup → command operation → evidence facts → reason-specific oracle. Preparation and every later load fail closed if a mapping is missing or if its actor, command, fact closure, setup isolation, expected outcome/error, or HTTP oracle diverges from the denominator. Its hash binds the current model, Blueprint, capability lock, Runtime Domain API, delivery, Runtime manifest, verification/package receipts, Runtime binary, and stable database cohort identity. The live process PID is intentionally not part of that stable hash because a restart case must replace it; the typed restart artifact must bind the old PID, current new PID, unchanged database cohort, delivery, and binary. A model, capability, source, package, database target, or Runtime change requires a new denominator; `prepare` archives every generation under `.domainry/builder/acceptance/history/denominator/`, and previously recorded results survive an evolution only through the incremental staleness flow below — never by assumption.

The denominator must cover every changed or newly published operation plus referenced prior evidence for unchanged operations. Each case names its Runtime owner, actor/role, permission and data scope, required outcome, error contract, restart sensitivity, and required evidence kinds. Every scoped read and write requires positive and differentiated-scope proof (database-agnostic, by ordinary query/HTTP probes — never engine-level RLS posture; see G14); every protected operation also requires permission-denied proof. Writes additionally require missing-idempotency-key rejection, idempotent replay, idempotency conflict, persistence read-back and audit correlation. Project Actions additionally require one HTTP mutation per business intent, one Runtime unit of work, atomic commit, injected rollback, and concurrency conflict; atomicity is proven by `http_exchange` + `transaction_trace` + `persistence_snapshot` + `audit_correlation`. The denominator never reads frontend source or requires frontend evidence. Each declared Handler Connector call gets its own case bound to the exact connector, connection, provider, operation, execution mode and side-effect class; durable writes require worker restart and terminal reconciliation. Declared notification events require after-commit once-only durable refetch, and every external channel gets its own provider-terminal case. Every Report and typed list/search/query operation requires bounded page and stable traversal cases with a query profile captured on the same database cohort named by the managed process receipt: SQLite uses `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, MySQL uses `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON`, and PostgreSQL uses `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`, all with statement/row-count observation and machine-checked index/full-scan classification. Evidence whose dialect or plan format differs from `runtime_identity.database_driver` is rejected; no second database or SQLite fallback is allowed. Its signed cursor must either encode the complete deterministic keyset tuple or bind an authorized source version to a bounded offset; a source-version-fenced continuation must reject source drift as a stale-cursor conflict. Automation Rules derive before-transaction rollback or after-commit restart/terminal cases from their trigger. Agent resources additionally require task cancel/retry/reconcile with terminal worker/audit evidence and interactive SSE disconnect/resume. A manual approval Workflow is proven as a durable process: start before the managed Runtime replacement, refetch after restart, decide real assigned tasks through participant APIs, and observe terminal persistence/audit; it does not claim `worker_terminal` unless the graph actually schedules worker-owned work. Scheduled jobs and governed report exports retain worker restart/resume evidence. Typed operations declared by acceptance `config.runtime_operations` must resolve to the pinned Runtime API and include both positive and denied rows for writes. Read and apply all 32 families in [production-technical-gates.md](production-technical-gates.md); a project may mark a family not applicable only from model-derived evidence.

Semantic oracles are strict. Each scenario uses fresh setup identities/records or names an explicit dependency whose passing evidence is current. A positive case must identify and observe its intended target with the required non-empty facts; a `2xx` paired with an empty collection, null result, zero aggregate, or different record is not proof unless that exact value is the confirmed outcome. A negative case must reach the intended stable status/error/concealment and prove unchanged durable state; an arbitrary `4xx`, `not found`, empty result caused by bad setup, or exception from a missing dependency is not the expected rejection. Scope isolation probes use otherwise equivalent requests against the same target through formal matching and non-matching Runtime sessions, plus the broader in-scope role when applicable. Runtime-owned identity/context values in setup and requests must come from the formal typed client, seed/admin path, or persisted Runtime result and be carried unchanged; synthetic claims or hand-normalized canonical values invalidate the case.

### Runner-first acceptance execution

With the denominator prepared and the managed Runtime healthy, execute the mechanical case families through the platform runner FIRST — before writing any harness code:

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance run --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --cases standard --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
```

The runner (capability `project.acceptance.run`, diagnostic report contract `domainry-backend-acceptance-run-v2`) mechanically executes the standard Action, Automation, Report GET-summary, Runtime read-route, Workflow, governed export and Scheduler families against the live Runtime and the exact sqlite/mysql/postgres database cohort bound by its managed process receipt, validates every artifact with the same `acceptance check` validators before writing it, and atomically writes/merges one complete `domainry-backend-acceptance-results-v2` document. External cohorts require the same explicit `DATABASE_DRIVER`/`DATABASE_DSN` environment binding already used by the managed Runtime; the runner compares only non-secret DSN/cohort identities and never serializes the DSN. It contains exactly one row per denominator case: `passed`, `declared_gap`, or `not_passed` with typed responsibility. Existing passed/gap rows are immutable; existing `not_passed` rows are retried. The separate `.domainry/development/acceptance-evidence/backend-acceptance-run.json` is execution diagnostics, not a second source of case truth. For every case the runner uses the semantic contract's exact actor and calls the authenticated Runtime `GET /identity/principal-context` resolver; Runtime returns canonical workspace/workforce/organization/business-profile/surface selectors, and the runner carries only those selectors into requests. Neither runner nor business harness may infer a user from role ordering, construct profile headers, or query Runtime-owned identity tables. Never re-implement or overwrite a runner-passed case. A `not_passed` outcome with `disposition:"runtime_failed"` is an observed contract violation — a product defect to repair at its owner, never a harness problem. Only `needs_business_harness` rows belong in the self-built harness. `blocked_dependency`, `blocked_platform`, `unsupported_runner`, `setup_failed`, `evidence_rejected`, and `runtime_failed` return to their named owner first; downstream cases sharing a failed setup are `blocked_dependency`, not independent failures.

Self-built harness code must be a thin assertion layer on top of [acceptance-harness-core.py](../assets/acceptance-harness-core.py): copy that file unchanged into `.domainry/development/`, then write only per-case assertion functions against it — never re-implement session/auth bootstrap, HTTP or database capture, artifact/evidence/results writers, resume state, retry/backoff plumbing, or any DSN parser/adapter. SQLite is stdlib-backed. For MySQL, install `PyMySQL` in the harness environment and call `AcceptanceDatabase.from_runtime_state(PROJECT_ROOT, state)` (or construct `Harness` normally) with no callback: core lazy-loads PyMySQL and exclusively accepts the managed Runtime Go-style contract `user:<password>@tcp(host:port)/database?charset=utf8mb4&parseTime=True&loc=Local`. URL DSNs, omitted or invalid targets/ports, and added, reordered, unknown, or dangerous query semantics fail closed; the password may be empty and is never emitted. Agent-written MySQL connectors and DSN parsers are prohibited. PostgreSQL retains the explicit advanced DB-API 2 `database_connector(driver, dsn, schema)` boundary. For both external drivers, core reads the random in-database marker and derives `sha256("domainry-managed-runtime-database-cohort-v1\n" + driver + "\n" + receipt.database_dsn_identity_sha256 + "\n" + marker_identity)` before comparing it with the managed Runtime receipt's `database_identity_sha256`; the marker is never itself the receipt identity, and copied marker rows at a different DSN identity fail closed. Missing or invalid receipt/marker contracts and identities are rejected without fallback. Core suppresses connector stdout/stderr, owns dialect SQL/EXPLAIN and DSN/password redaction, and never falls back to SQLite. Use `harness.session_for_case(case)` exclusively for the frozen actor/principal mapping. Register cases in `ScenarioGraph`; each setup receives a fresh opaque namespace, `setup_failed` is distinct from a product failure, and downstream cases become `blocked_dependency` rather than executing against missing residue. Apply `ReasonOracle` for exact positive, rejection, state, scope, and audit assertions before sealing evidence.

Execute only the remaining `needs_business_harness` cases through that real acceptance harness and project-provisioned non-human Runtime identities. The harness—not prose editing—writes typed HTTP exchanges, SSE transcripts, durable refetches, idempotency receipts, database snapshots, transaction and pagination traces, query profiles, audit correlation, differentiated-scope data, provider receipts, worker terminal observations, and restart observations under project-owned `backend/tests/evidence/**`. Self-built harness code and every intermediate working file live under `.domainry/development/**` from the very first file, never anywhere under `backend/**`: harness files inside `backend/**` dirty the finalized `source_sha256` and make every gate receipt stale, and the measured cost of that mistake is a full finalize/verify/package redo plus re-recording all evidence. Every structured observation references one real regular non-symlink artifact and its SHA-256; persistence evidence also supplies before/after hashes and, for replay, the replay hash. Results and every evidence document bind the denominator and Runtime identity hashes. Then run:

The result document contract is `domainry-backend-acceptance-results-v2`: copy `denominator_sha256`, `runtime_identity`, and `runtime_identity_sha256` exactly from the denominator and provide exactly one `results[]` row for every denominator case. A `passed` row contains `case_id`, `state`, and `evidence[]` (`path`, `sha256`); a `not_passed` row contains no evidence and requires `outcome.disposition`, stable `code`, `owner`, `root_case_id`, `retryable`, and factual `reason`; a `declared_gap` row uses the existing typed gap contract. `acceptance check` fails closed while any `not_passed` row remains. The business harness may replace only a row whose disposition is `needs_business_harness`; it cannot replace platform, dependency, setup, evidence, unsupported-runner, or Runtime failures. Each referenced evidence document is `domainry-backend-acceptance-evidence-v1` with `state:"passed"`, the exact case/denominator/Runtime hashes, and `observations[]`. An observation has `kind`, project-relative `artifact`, `artifact_sha256`, and only for `persistence_snapshot` the required `before_sha256`/`after_sha256` plus replay SHA when applicable. Each artifact is strict JSON `domainry-backend-acceptance-artifact-v1` and binds its kind, case, operation, Runtime identity, producer source receipt, capture owner, and typed facts. Accepted kinds are `http_exchange`, `persistence_snapshot`, `idempotency_receipt`, `sse_transcript`, `durable_refetch`, `runtime_restart`, `worker_terminal`, `differentiated_scope_data`, `transaction_trace`, `pagination_trace`, `query_profile`, `audit_correlation`, `security_posture`, and `provider_receipt`. Pagination facts bind stable sort/tie-breaker and cursor strategy; offset fencing additionally requires the bound source version and observed stale-cursor rejection. Provider receipts bind the denominator's exact connector, connection, provider, operation; a durable provider or notification audit also requires its outbox reference. A correctly hashed arbitrary text file or a typed artifact whose endpoint, actor, outcome, transaction counts, page facts, process/database identity, differentiated data scope, or provider terminal state contradicts the denominator is rejected. The harness must preserve secrets safely, but redaction cannot remove facts needed to prove the case.

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance check --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
```

The check reruns model derivation, resolves the live managed Runtime cohort, verifies every raw artifact, and requires exact set equality with the denominator. Missing, orphan, duplicate, failed, stale, unbound, unknown-kind, artifactless, or `self_reported` coverage fails. A percentage, prose claim, Mock transcript, or evidence from another Runtime can never satisfy it.

### Incremental re-recording after a model evolution

The denominator's `artifact_manifest` digests each operation's dependency closure, so an evolution no longer forces a blind full re-record: evidence recorded against an archived earlier generation stays binding when a complete hash proof chain shows nothing its case depends on changed. After any evolution, with the new denominator prepared, first run:

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance stale-report --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
```

The report (contract `domainry-backend-acceptance-stale-report-v1`) classifies every case as `current` (evidence still binds), `stale` (with reason), `missing`, or `declared_gap`, plus counts. Re-record ONLY the `stale` + `missing` subset. For the runner's mechanical families, re-run `project acceptance run --cases standard` on the same results file: it applies the same per-case carry-forward proof, keeps every `current` result (report field `carried_forward`), rebinds the file to the new denominator, and re-executes only what it dropped. For the remaining stale business-assertion cases, re-record through the harness core's stale-list resume — `stale_case_ids(<stale-report>)` plus `Harness(..., stale_report=...)` and `pending_cases(...)` — which rewrites only the affected result entries (evidence file paths are reused) instead of rebuilding the results file. Then run `acceptance check` as usual: a receipt with non-zero `carried_forward_cases` is a normal, complete result — carried-forward coverage is hash-proven, never a gap and never `self_reported`.

Carry-forward pays only when the repair converges on attributable model items (actions, workflows, reports, export controls, scheduled jobs, agent tasks — plus a report's own `backend/reports/<report-key>.sql`). Any other project source change — handler code, config, anything else under `backend/**` — and any shared-collection change (objects, roles, workspaces, automation rules, seeds, ...) shifts the shared digest and makes every case stale; prefer model-item-level fixes and keep every working file out of `backend/**` (harness location discipline above).

Finish the complete verification round before repair. Preserve every first failure and continue safe checks to collect the full finding inventory. `reconcile` never replays a product command and never overwrites a stale declared pass with a failed attempt: a strictly verifiable legacy cohort may receive an explicit migration receipt, a prior pass may be restored only from intact authoritative evidence, and every other case enters the typed manual repair queue. Recoverable `repair_required` exits 0 for shell continuation; only typed unrecoverable or corrupted/unsafe input exits nonzero. Then repair the named owner, create new round-specific Gates for invalidated commands, and continue; a terminal Gate and its first receipt are never overwritten or rerun.

The CLI makes this concrete for local structural checks. A failed metadata checklist writes `.domainry/builder/receipts/checklist-failed.json`; a failed source finalization writes `.domainry/builder/receipts/finalization-failed.json`; a failed `project verify` writes `.domainry/builder/receipts/verification-failed.json`. Each check is `passed`, `failed`, or `skipped_dependency`. Safe independent checks run in the same round even when a sibling fails; dependency-bound checks are skipped explicitly. Treat every `failed` row as one repair inventory and never treat `skipped_dependency` as a pass. These receipts remain L1 structural evidence only.

Acceptance in this Skill verifies backend logic end-to-end — real managed-Runtime HTTP/SSE/worker/database behavior. Browser-layer UI verification is outside its acceptance scope and is never a completion precondition.

The evidence Gate must bind evidence content plus applicable source, model/Blueprint, and Runtime identities. A later identity or artifact-content change makes the Gate stale. Re-run commands or regenerate artifacts; never reattach unchanged prose.

Evidence rules — tool-produced content only: every evidence file's content must be produced by a command, script, or platform tool and carry what makes it reproducible (the recorded command line, or its source plus sha256). The model never hand-transcribes, excerpts, or re-arranges content into an evidence file. In the TODO, an `Evidence:` line carries only the gate ID and path pointers; inlining more than one line of content there is prohibited.

## Failure classification

- Missing credentials, acceptance identities, differentiated data, explicit Runtime configuration, routes, permissions, sessions, Runtime health, or persistence is normally an implementation/Foundation defect. Return it to its owner and repair it in the same session; it becomes an external blocker only when every authorized provisioning/recovery path remains unavailable with recorded evidence.
- `verification_blocked` is allowed only when implementation is complete and every authorized execution mechanism for a required check remains unavailable after all recovery paths, or when continuing would risk data corruption/security, a result-changing business ambiguity has no safe authority, or governing contracts are objectively contradictory. Name the blocked checks, recovery attempts, project-local/external evidence, and highest reached level.
- Missing, partial, skipped, failed, stale, unbound, contradictory, or insufficient behavior evidence from an ordinary round is a repair finding, not a blocker, task exit, or intentional prototype. It can become terminal `acceptance_failed` only after every evidence-supported in-scope owner repair has been exhausted and the same frozen contract still fails.
- A non-blocking limitation may be reported only when it is outside the frozen scope and does not weaken an in-scope claim.

## Terminal states

This terminal verification sequence applies to `Execution scope: implementation`. A `requirements_only` batch may move directly from closed requirements/domain-truth Gates to `done`; that state proves only the accepted requirements artifact, reports no delivery or L1-L5 implementation claim, and must not imply Runtime or UI verification.

Record exactly one state:

- `done`: every in-scope Gate has current bound evidence at the required level, the acceptance matrix is complete, the finding inventory is empty, and no requirement is hidden, downgraded, or deferred.
- `acceptance_failed`: after the same-session repair loop exhausts every evidence-supported in-scope owner repair, implementation or evidence still fails the frozen acceptance contract. A first or ordinary failed acceptance round never qualifies.
- `verification_blocked`: implementation is complete but a required check cannot execute because no authorized execution capability exists.

Only `done` permits a whole-batch completion claim. Other states report per-capability results and the highest evidence level without upward summarization. Neither state is a shortcut around diagnosis: do not record it merely because validate/apply/verify/package/Runtime/canary/acceptance returned non-zero, and do not move a recoverable repair to user wait or another Host/Agent session.

Before completion, keep `Current stage: verify`, require the evidence Gate's `verify` status to pass, and run the TODO checker with `--expected-stage verify`. Change the stage to `done` only after terminal policy permits it; then require the Gate's `done` status and run the TODO checker again immediately before the final response.

The final summary states terminal state, implemented scope, frontend mutation scope, current delivery identity, tests/builds, Runtime result, highest evidence level, restart result, and open limitations. Never imply L4 browser evidence — it is outside this Skill's acceptance scope.

# M1 Benchmark:销售线索 CRM 需求规格

本文档是 benchmark 的唯一需求输入。评分对照 golden-checklist(agent 不可见)。

## 业务背景

一家 B2B 公司的销售团队管理线索(lead)到成交客户(customer)的全流程:销售录入并跟进线索,大额转化需销售总监审批,团队按部门划分数据边界,管理层看漏斗报表并导出。

## 组织与角色

- 销售分属**部门**(至少两个部门:华东区、华北区),存在汇报线。
- **sales_rep(销售)**:录入/跟进自己名下的线索;可见范围=本部门线索;发起转化。
- **sales_director(销售总监)**:全部门可见;审批大额转化;查看/导出漏斗报表。

## 功能需求

### 线索管理
1. 线索字段:公司名(必填)、联系人、联系电话、预计金额(精确金额,两位小数)、来源(select:官网/展会/转介绍/外呼)、状态、负责人(销售)、部门、创建/更新时间。
2. 线索状态机:`new → contacted → qualified → converted / lost`;`qualified` 可标记 `lost`;`converted`、`lost` 为终态,不可再转换。
3. 销售创建线索(初始 new,负责人=本人,部门=本人部门);可更新自己名下线索的联系人/电话/预计金额/来源。
4. 跟进(contacted)与合格判定(qualified)由负责人执行;状态只能沿定义的转换变化。
5. 线索创建幂等(相同幂等键重复提交只建一条)。

### 转化与审批(核心业务)
6. 负责人对 `qualified` 线索发起**转化**:预计金额 < 100000 时直接转化;≥ 100000 时必须进入**审批流**,由 sales_director 审批。
7. 审批通过:线索进入 `converted`,并在**同一事务**中创建 `customer` 客户记录(承接公司名/联系人/金额/来源线索引用);审批拒绝:线索回到 `qualified` 并记录拒绝原因。
8. 转化必须幂等:同一线索重复发起转化不产生第二个客户。
9. 审批结果(通过/拒绝)以站内通知发给发起的销售。
10. 客户记录只读(任何角色不可更新/删除客户;修正走新流程,本期不做)。

### 数据边界
11. 销售的线索可见范围 = **本部门**(同部门同事的线索可见,跨部门不可见);更新/状态操作仅限**自己名下**。
12. 总监全量可见。
13. 所有状态变化与转化审批留审计。

### 跟进提醒(定时)
14. 每天早上(工作日)由**定时任务**扫描:`contacted` 状态超过 7 天未变化的线索,给负责人发站内提醒(每条线索每天最多提醒一次)。

### 报表与导出
15. 总监可见**漏斗报表**:按状态统计线索数与预计金额合计;销售无权查看。
16. 总监可**导出线索明细 CSV**(带当前权限过滤);导出必须走受控导出通道(有界、审计、requester 专属)。
17. 线索列表服务端有界分页。

### 导航与验收
18. 两角色登录 Business Workspace 后菜单与权限一致(销售:我的线索;总监:全部线索、报表)。
19. 提供两个部门 × 各 1 名销售 + 1 名总监的非人类验收身份,以及覆盖所有状态、两个部门、含 ≥100000 与 <100000 金额的种子线索(≥6 条),保证每条需求可在真实 Runtime 验证。

## 范围限定

仅 Business Workspace;无 Consumer Portal、无外部连接器;金额计算只做求和,不涉及分成/结算。

This one TODO and Host/Agent session own every normal repair round through complete acceptance. After first executions, invoke the Gate runner's `reconcile --cli "$DOMAINRY_CLI"`; it validates current receipts, performs only strictly proven identity migration/reuse, generates exact requirement coverage, and returns the complete typed repair queue. It never replays a product command (effectful or read-only) and never changes a stale declared pass to failed. `done` and recoverable `repair_required` both emit complete JSON, exit 0, and keep `agent_should_stop:false`; only typed unrecoverable or corrupted/unsafe contract input exits nonzero with `agent_should_stop:true`. Repair the queue and invoke it again in this session until `state:"done"`.

For `requirements_only`, keep only the header, these rules, `requirements`, `domain truth design`, and `done`; record model/apply/Runtime/verify omission in the header and never claim delivery, integration, or L1-L5 implementation evidence. Bind Gate evidence with `--bind requirements` to the deterministic evidence closure: mandatory non-empty `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md`, root `requirements.md` when present, and the non-derived regular files under `frontend/**` when `frontend/src/**` proves a frontend exists. A frontend-led or immutable external-reference PRD may omit root `requirements.md`; it records the authority plus immutable snapshot/commit or citation, and the frontend closure is included automatically. Never guess `--bind source`. After `list` supplies the Gate ID, direct artifact closure uses `attach --gate-id <gate-id> --status passed --evidence-type source_artifact --evidence-path docs/backend-requirements-prd.md --bind requirements`, and validator closure uses `run --gate-id <gate-id> --bind requirements -- <validator argv>`. Validation commands use no pipeline or set `pipefail` inside the executed shell before the pipeline, so an internal failure cannot be masked by `tee`. For an implementation light batch, instantiate only the sections the batch touches per the batch-scale rules in development-guide.md (always keep `verify` and `done`; record every omission in `Sections omitted` with the prior accepted evidence reference; never omit or close as not applicable anything the batch touches; reclassify as full and copy the missing sections back if a light criterion breaks mid-batch).

Keep the `(only-if-expected-invalid-check)` item only when the prepared source state makes the first `project check` genuinely expected to return a repair inventory; otherwise delete it. If that expectation becomes concrete after `project source prepare`, insert the item in its physical position immediately before the valid-check Gate before executing the check. # Domainry Plane boundary

V2 uses Domainry Plane only through the single packaged `domainry-cli` executable.

Choose one explicit `--environment <local|dev|stage|online>` or `--service <url>` target for `model apply` and Connector definition discovery. Keep that target fixed for the batch.

Release only with:

```text
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module> --product-surfaces <reviewed-surfaces> [one target]
```

The command converges `backend/model/*.json`, checks the complete model, validates it with Domainry Plane, publishes the immutable delivery, materializes or evolves the backend, and finalizes source. For an existing Builder delivery change, inspect the first run's immutable evolution audit, then run the same product command through a new round-specific Gate with `--evolution-audit-sha256 <emitted-sha256> --evolution-reason <reviewed-reason>`. A stale audit fails closed. Repair any other failed input or stage and use a new Gate for the next run.

Do not call Domainry Plane directly, reconstruct signing, hand-edit delivery state, or invent separate validate/publish/materialize commands. The current Builder flow keeps reviewed evolution inside `model apply`; it exposes no neighboring delivery-maintenance command surface.
# Project-owned source

Git owns project source. Edit, format, test, rename, and delete backend project source with normal development tools while preserving unrelated work. `frontend/**` remains read-only under every `Frontend mutation scope` (the scope records authorization context only): evidence that assigns a defect to the frontend produces a finding with owner `frontend`, never an edit.

Allowed backend source includes `backend/go.mod`, `backend/go.sum`, `backend/actions/**`, `backend/config/**`, `backend/connectors/**`, `backend/domain/**`, `backend/i18n/**`, and `backend/tests/**`. Never edit `frontend/**`, `backend/generated/**`, `backend/cmd/**`, frozen contracts, Runtime manifests, receipts, caches, journals, packages, or other `.domainry/**` state. The only writable `.domainry` exception is the current session's `.domainry/development/<session-id>.md` TODO.

For an approved Action source gap:

1. Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project source prepare --json --project <project>` once for the current delivery. It validates every delivered Action context, creates only missing canonical Handler/test skeletons in batches of at most 32 files, atomically persists one immutable content-addressed `implementation_packet` under managed `.domainry/builder/**`, and returns only a bounded envelope. Existing regular files are `unchanged`; a symlink, duplicate path, unknown context contract, or changed materialization baseline fails closed. Retain the exact returned `.implementation_packet.path` plus its delivery/materialization identity and payload/file hashes; never reconstruct it, redirect stdout to create it, or use `latest.json`. Read the envelope's small Action key/path/state index first, then locally select one packet Action with `jq --arg action_key ... '.actions[] | select(.action_key == $action_key)'` and only a needed document with `jq --arg sha256 ... '.documents[] | select(.sha256 == $sha256) | .content'`. Never `cat` or print the complete packet and do not reload the installed batch Action by Action.
2. Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" action context --projection coding --project <project> [--evolution-audit-sha256 <sha256>] <object>.<action>` only for a genuinely isolated repair or an Action that exists only in a pending delivery evolution. Supply the exact reviewed audit SHA for the latter.
3. Optionally run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" action scaffold apply --json --project <project> [--evolution-audit-sha256 <sha256>] --expected-source-sha256 <sha256|absent> --expected-test-sha256 <sha256|absent> --template <id> <object>.<action>`.
4. Submit the complete Handler and test atomically with `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" action source apply --json --project <project> [--evolution-audit-sha256 <sha256>] --expected-source-sha256 <sha256|absent> --expected-test-sha256 <sha256|absent> --input - <object>.<action>`. Context, scaffold, and source apply must use the same audit SHA so their target delivery and CAS scope cannot drift.

The batch-prepared skeleton compiles against the delivered capability types but intentionally returns `*.not_implemented`. It exposes missing implementation coverage early; it is never positive-path evidence. When the Handler is implemented, replace the paired generated test's nil Execution call and `*.not_implemented` oracle with typed non-nil Execution/capability stubs and assertions over current outputs and business effects; a generic no-panic assertion is not meaningful behavior evidence.

For an approved Connector source gap, load `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" connector context --projection coding --project <project> <connector>.<provider>` and optionally apply the generated scaffold with `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" connector scaffold apply --json --project <project> --expected-source-sha256 <sha256|absent> --expected-test-sha256 <sha256|absent> <connector>.<provider>`. Implement the remaining project-owned Connector source directly under `backend/connectors/**`.

After the current module's source/tests are implemented and every preceding implementation TODO item is closed, run its module-focused Go tests through the Gate runner before source finalization. Then run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project check --json --scope actions --project <project>` and require exit 0 before `project source finalize`. The check statically scans delivery-bound canonical Action test paths and the production Action source. An implemented Handler paired with a generated test that still has nil Execution or an exact `*.not_implemented` oracle returns `state:"invalid"` plus a bounded, stable diagnostic inventory; ordinary hand-written nil robustness tests are not generated-scaffold matches. Source-policy and applicable Go compile failures also return contract-shaped bounded JSON. Finalize repeats those preflights and writes only its failure receipt on failure. Cross-module/full verification tests, verification, packaging, and Runtime start require the current successful finalization. A Gate is terminal after its first passed or failed receipt; after repair, add a new round-specific Gate to the same session TODO, sync, rerun the affected command, and continue rather than ending or replacing the Host/Agent session.
# Authorization and behavior ownership

Keep Action invocation, object permission, data scope, field policy, Surface access, assurance, and execution ownership separate.

- Give every Handler Action exactly one execution owner and exact `allowed_roles`.
- Use `object_operation` when no existing record ID is supplied; use `record_operation` only for a caller-supplied existing record.
- Declare every `list`, `get`, `get_for_update`, `create`, `update`, `conditional_update`, delete/restore, and Connector capability used by the algorithm. Locking is not mutation authority.
- Put volatile correctness invariants in generated conditional mutation and preserve its typed conflict error when required. Do not replace concurrency semantics with a friendly precheck.
- Grant relation-target reads and narrow data scope explicitly. A display reference permission is not target read permission.
- Keep direct CRUD permission separate from Handler EffectAuthority. Never widen a business role merely to collect audit evidence.
- Before the single live validation, compute Handler EffectAuthority for every `(Action, allowed_role, data_access)` tuple. Every allowed role needs a non-empty data scope on each referenced Object, with `read: true` for `get`, `get_for_update`, `optional`, `list`, `exists`, or `count`, and `write: true` for `create`, `update`, `conditional_update`, `delete`, or `restore`. The role does not need direct CRUD permission merely because the Handler holds EffectAuthority, but missing data scope still fails compilation.
- Validate that complete matrix once across all Handlers; do not wait for live validation to reveal one missing role/Object grant at a time. Narrow `allowed_roles` only when the PRD actor truly must not execute the Action, never as a shortcut around EffectAuthority.
- After backend implementation and real Runtime/database data acceptance, count every published Action and persist TODO matrix rows with delta scope: for a full batch, one row per published Action with total Actions equal to matrix rows; for an existing-project increment, one row per Action added or changed in this batch plus summary rows that reference the prior accepted matrix evidence for unchanged Actions, with authored plus referenced rows still covering the published total. When a light batch changes no Action, role, permission, scope, or menu, omit this acceptance from the instantiated TODO with the omission recorded in the header, or close it as not applicable with scope evidence referencing the prior accepted matrices and totals instead of re-authoring rows. Record target, permission or exact `allowed_roles`, data scope, allowed and denied probes, current Runtime/persistence evidence, and result. Zero unowned or untested Actions is the backend completion condition.
- Treat Action creation and its Role authorization as one modeling change. Before moving to the next Action, add its truthful `authorization.allowed_roles`, the matching scoped `data_permissions` for every Handler access and declared project relation target, and positive/denied acceptance actors. Checklist aggregates `compose.action_role_authorization_missing`, `compose.action_role_data_permission_missing`, and `compose.action_role_relation_target_read_missing`; repair the full Action/Role/Object set together. For non-Handler Actions, at least one declared role must hold the published `permission`; Handler grant derivation is owned by [actions-and-transactions](capabilities/actions-and-transactions.md).
- Model one positive allowed scenario, role-denied scenario, and when relevant sibling/out-of-scope concealed scenario.

- Treat Runtime-derived organization claims and Product Surface identity as trusted Runtime facts, never request input or guessed headers.
